related_questions.question: Do you need antibiotics for upper respiratory infection?

text_blocks.snippet: Most upper respiratory infections (URIs) are caused by viruses and don't require antibiotics. Antibiotics are only effective against bacterial infections, and most URIs are viral. If a URI is caused by bacteria, antibiotics may be prescribed, but this is less common.
snippet_highlighted_words: Most upper respiratory infections (URIs) are caused by viruses and don't require antibiotics

list.snippet: The common cold, most sore throats, and most sinus infections are caused by viruses.
Antibiotics are not effective against viruses, so they won't help with these infections.
Most viral URIs will resolve on their own within 1-2 weeks.
Home remedies and over-the-counter medications can help manage symptoms.
Some URIs, like strep throat, can be caused by bacteria.
If a doctor suspects a bacterial infection, they may prescribe antibiotics.
If antibiotics are prescribed, it's important to take the full course as directed, even if symptoms improve.
If symptoms worsen after 7-10 days, according to Keck Medicine of USC.
If symptoms include a persistent fever (over 100.4°F or 38°C).
If you have difficulty breathing or chest pain.
If you have symptoms of a secondary bacterial infection, like a sinus infection or pneumonia.
If you have symptoms that are severe or not improving with home care.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: Antibiotics should only be used when a bacterial infection is suspected or confirmed, as overuse can lead to antibiotic resistance, according to Johns Hopkins Medicine.

text_blocks.snippet: An upper respiratory tract infection (URI), or upper respiratory infection, is a common illness that affects the nose, throat, and airways. It's usually caused by viruses and includes symptoms like a runny or stuffy nose, sore throat, cough, and sometimes fever. While most URIs resolve on their own within a couple of weeks, treatment focuses on relieving symptoms.
snippet_highlighted_words: a common illness that affects the nose, throat, and airways

list.snippet: URIs are infections of the upper respiratory tract, which includes the nasal passages, sinuses, throat (pharynx), and larynx.
The most common cause is viral infection, such as rhinoviruses, adenoviruses, and influenza viruses.
In some cases, bacteria can also be responsible.
Symptoms can vary but often include:
Runny or stuffy nose
Sore throat
Cough
Sneezing
Slight fever
Fatigue
URIs are contagious and spread through respiratory droplets produced when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or by touching contaminated surfaces and then touching the face.
Most URIs are self-limiting and resolve within a couple of weeks.
Treatment focuses on relieving symptoms such as:
Rest
Hydration
Over-the-counter medications for pain and fever
Saline nasal sprays or drops to relieve congestion
Sore throat lozenges or sprays
Cool mist vaporizers
Antibiotics are generally not effective against viral infections and are only prescribed for bacterial infections.
